data.reasoning: The only valid, non-advisory report (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all files and found no malicious code. The PKGBUILD downloads pinned binaries from the official Azul CDN, and the install script uses standard Arch Linux Java management tools. The inconclusive result from qwen3 was due to API errors (HTTP 400), not actual security concerns, and the openrouter report is advisory only.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool failures rather than analytical differences. The qwen3 model crashed with HTTP 400 errors when attempting to audit the PKGBUILD and install script, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The openrouter model failed to parse the desktop file due to non-standard output formatting. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and correctly identified the package as safe.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit PKGBUILD and jre25-zulu-bin.install due to HTTP 400 API errors, resulting in an incomplete review.
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for LLM API errors (e.g., HTTP 400) to prevent entire file audits from failing and skewing the final verdict to inconclusive.
Improve the output parser to be more resilient to non-standard or malformed XML/tags from cheaper or smaller models, such as handling plain text safety declarations instead of strict <decision> tags.
